List revised.

4. The present revision under Sections 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the revisionist- Sushil Kumar against the judgement and order dated 07.02.2009 passed by learned Sessions Judge,
Auraiya in Criminal Appeal No. 06 of 2007 (Sushil Kumar Vs. under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, P.S.- Dibiyapur, District Auraiya,
whereby, the revisionist has been convicted under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 for 06 months simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/- and in default to deposit the fine 02 months additional simple imprisonment which has also been affirmed by the appellate court.

sentences.text: 5. The facts of the case are that N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector found the revisionist on 30.11.2002 at about 12.00 p.m. at Nahar Bazar, Dibiyapur, District Auraiya, while he was selling pede (sweet made of khoya) without license.

The food Inspector introduced himself and purchased 600 gm of pede from the revisionist by giving Rs. 42/- for sample and then kept in three plastic in equal quantity and after labelling it affixed seal on it which was then sent to the public analyst for chemical analysis and the chemical analyst after analysis found the sample to be adulterated in which starch was found.
The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused.
In the trial court the complainant N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector was examined as P.W.-1, Kush Kumar Gupta, Food Clerk was examined as PW-2.
The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication.
The trial court convicted and sentenced the accused/revisionist as stated above.
The appeal was preferred against the same which came to be dismissed after which the present revision has been filed against both the impugned judgement and orders.
6. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that N.R. Pandey, the Food Inspector was examined as P.W.-1 under Section 244 Cr.P.C. and states of taking sample of pede from the revisionist.
It is further argued that the notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has not been received by the revisionist.

It is argued that there is nothing on record to show that the same as has been sent by the Food Inspector has been received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated.

To buttress the arguments learned counsel has placed the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs.
State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9).

entities.text:
Vijendra vs.
State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that in the trial P.W.-2 Kush Kumar Gupta, the Food Clerk although states of sending notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act through the registered post but also states that he has no information regarding the receipt of the same by the accused.

It is argued that the trial court while dealing with the said issue although has stated that the said witness has not referred to and stated regarding the fact of receipt of the said notice by the accused but the accused has not produced any evidence from his side which would go to show that he has not received any notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act.

The said finding is incomplete and would not stand to the test of the view as held by the Apex Court in the above two judgement in as much as the trial court is expected to return a specific finding regarding the receipt of the notice by the accused.

Since there is no such affirmative finding by the trial court regarding receipt of the notice notice u/s 13 (2) of the Act by the accused-revisionist it cannot be said that the said notice was received by him.

It is argued that the present revision thus deserved to be allowed.
7.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.

The appellate court has also considered the Sushil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95810770/
2 matter in its true prospective and has come to a conclusion that the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
8.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, in the matter since the there is nothing on record to show that the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act has been received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated.
9. The present revision is allowed.

The impugned judgement and 07.02.2009 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Auraiya and the judgement and order dated 12.07.2007 passed by the Special /
Chief Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offence), Auraiya in the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.

Chief Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offence), Auraiya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 10. The revisionist is acquitted of the charges levelled against him.
The revisionist is reported to be in jail after being arrested in compliance of the order dated 02.11.2023 passed by this Court issuing non-bailable warrants against him.
He shall be released from jail forthwith unless wanted in any other case.
11. Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement along with the trial court records to the concerned trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
12. The file be consigned to records.
Order on Criminal Misc. Recall Application No. 1 of 2023 1.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Recall Application No. 1 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that due to non appearance on behalf of the revisionist or his counsel, non bailable warrants were issued against him vide order dated 02.11.2023 and as such he prays that the said order be recalled and the revisionist be enlarged on bail.
2. In view of the same, the present recall application stands disposed of in terms of the order passed in the aforesaid Criminal Revision No. 599 of 2009 (Sushil Kumar vs. State of U.P. and Another).
